svg.title: TCIA: choose the right labels
svg.desc: Curator guide separating dataset disease and primary site from download category, data type and payload format. Verify NCIt and UBERON mappings, reuse faithful existing labels, and question any unconfirmed new WordPress value.
svg.text: Describe the cohort. Then classify each downloadable component.
What condition does the cohort represent, and where did it originate?
Match the diagnosis and its supported specificity.
Keep the NCIt code, definition and mapping evidence.
A study context may need explicit curator review.
Use the known primary disease site.
Scanned anatomy and metastatic sites are separate.
Keep the UBERON ID and mapping evidence.
Check all three fields independently for every download.
What broad role does it serve?
Use the NCI Imaging Submission Model and GDC schemas
to guide meaning; their enums do not authorize TCIA terms.
03 WHEN A VALUE IS NEW OR UNCERTAIN
Pause that assignment: needs curator decision
Question any value not confirmed in the same WordPress field — including category, type and format.
Show the evidence, closest existing terms, why they do not fit, and the proposed definition / code.
Unseen in published usage does not prove absent from WordPress. Check the term registry.
If ontology, registry or content evidence is unavailable, record the check as unable to verify.
Prior use ≠ semantic verification ≠ registry membership
Vocabulary examples: validated 9 October 2026 snapshot; current registry and latest release not verified.
No automatic WordPress changes. Full policy, observed labels and source links accompany this graphic.
Sources: NCI EVS / caDSR · UBERON via EMBL-EBI OLS · NCI Imaging Submission Model · GDC · TCIA branding
